prompt_text:
You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw.

## Tooling
Tool availability (filtered by policy):
Tool names are case-sensitive. Call tools exactly as listed.
- gmail_list_messages: List inbox messages
- gmail_get_message: Get one message
When a first-class tool exists for an action, use the tool directly.

## Tool Schemas
Complete JSON Schema for available tools:
- gmail_list_messages
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "days_back": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 60
    },
    "max_results": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 30
    }
  },
  "required": []
}
```
- gmail_get_message
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "message_id"
  ]
}
```

## Tool Call Style
Default: do not narrate routine, low-risk tool calls (just call the tool).
Narrate only when it helps: multi-step work, complex tasks, or sensitive actions.
Keep narration brief and value-dense.
Tool-call protocol is strict: use native API tool/function calls only.
Never emit tool calls as plain text markup (for example: <tool_call>, <function=...>, <parameter=...>).
If a tool is needed, issue a real tool call block instead of describing or simulating it in text.

## Safety
- Safety: No independent objective; do not pursue self-preservation, replication, or resource acquisition.
- Tool Call Style: For low-risk actions, call tools directly without narration; narrate only for complex tasks.
- Reply Tags: Use [[reply_to_current]] to control reply relationship when needed.
- Silent Reply: If no reply is needed, output NO_REPLY.
- Heartbeat: Heartbeat checks should return HEARTBEAT_OK when no action is needed.

## Skills (mandatory)
Before replying: scan <available_skills> entries.
- If exactly one skill clearly applies: read its SKILL.md using the configured read tool, then follow it.
- If multiple skills could apply: choose the most specific one, then read and follow it.
- If none clearly apply: do not read any SKILL.md.
Constraints: never read more than one skill up front; only read after selecting.
The full SKILL.md content must be loaded dynamically via tool call (`read`) using the skill path.
<available_skills>
</available_skills>

## Workspace Files (injected)

Using the retrieved emails, produce an English stakeholder alignment status report with these sections:
1) Project Overview
2) Role-based progress (Delivery/Engineering/Support/Customer Success) — summarize the key points from each role
3) Dependencies and Risks — explicitly call out where progress depends on other teams and what might block outcomes
4) Items requiring executive/management confirmation — list at least 3 actionable items
5) Current Status — reconcile inconsistencies by incorporating the latest information and the “metrics definition changed / communication correction” email if present, then provide a single aligned final status.

Explicitly identify at least two places where different role emails disagree on status, and resolve them into a unified final narrative in the “Current Status” section.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Delivery Update: Integration Acceptance Window
response_body.body:
Team, as of today Project Alpha integration is NOT yet accepted by QA. Engineering says core APIs are ready, but the integration acceptance window is still open: we have to complete verification of event flows end-to-end (orders -> dashboard -> webhooks). Proposed acceptance window: 07/15-07/17. If QA sign-off slips, our customer rollout will need a date adjustment.

Next steps: please confirm the integration test environment is stable and provide the exact checklist for the handoff so delivery can coordinate with support for readiness.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Engineering Check-in: Core APIs Stabilized
response_body.body:
Good news: by 07/06 the core API surface for Project Alpha is stable in staging. We completed integration test runs for the primary endpoints (auth + metrics read + export). No new regressions after the last WebSocket gateway patch.

Remaining engineering work is limited to documentation polish and tightening alert thresholds. Engineering can support the integration acceptance checklist, but we need delivery to lock the QA window so we can staff on-call.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Support Concern: Post-Launch Ticket Volume Prep
response_body.body:
We’re worried about support readiness for Project Alpha launch. Based on prior dashboards, we expect a spike in migration/help requests and incident reports during the first 72 hours.

Current gaps:
- We do not yet have the runbook for “export endpoint throttling” and “WebSocket reconnect behavior”.
- The customer-facing troubleshooting flow is not final.
- We need confirmation on the estimated rollout timing so we can ensure on-call coverage and training.

Please share: rollout schedule + the top 5 known issues with mitigations.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Customer Success Sync: Training & Migration Assistance
response_body.body:
CS update: customer calls are progressing for Project Alpha, but we need an early confirmation on training + migration help.

What we told customers:
- Training sessions start the week before rollout.
- Migration assistance is included for the first two cycles.

What we still need internally:
1) confirm whether training is “recorded + live Q&A” or live-only
2) confirm the migration assistance window (days) and who provides escalation
3) align on one message for readiness: customers are hearing different timelines from different internal teams.

If we can’t align by 07/13, CS will pause new scheduling requests to avoid contradicting messaging.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Comms: Shared Uptime Dashboard Link
response_body.body:
FYI for Project Alpha stakeholders: the shared uptime dashboard is https://alpha-status.mycompany.internal (requires SSO). Please use it as the single source of truth for incident monitoring during rollout.

If you see discrepancies, escalate with timestamp + service name so we can correlate. Do not base ticket volume assumptions on internal estimates alone.

response_body.subject: Re: Project Alpha Integration Acceptance — Checklist Details
response_body.body:
Acceptance checklist for Project Alpha integration (for QA sign-off):
- Auth handshake completes for 3 test tenants
- Metrics read returns correct counts for baseline dataset
- Export endpoint returns expected file format for 2 scenarios
- WebSocket gateway reconnect within 10s recovers stream
- Audit log entries exist for all actions above

We can run the checklist during 07/15-07/17 as long as staging remains consistent. Please ensure Engineering does not introduce schema changes during this window.

response_body.subject: Metrics Definition Correction: Project Alpha “Success Rate” Calculation
response_body.body:
Correction / alignment notice (important): our previously reported “Success Rate” for Project Alpha used an inconsistent metrics definition.

What changed:
- Old definition (used in earlier status emails): Success Rate = successful events / all events observed in gateway logs.
- New definition (now adopted): Success Rate = successful user sessions / total authenticated sessions (excludes failed auth).

Impact:
- The old metric will look lower in environments with auth failures.
- Engineering’s staging numbers and Support’s production ticket correlates were comparing different denominators.

Going forward:
- Use the new definition for all stakeholder reporting.
- When discussing stability, separate “API success” from “session success”.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Engineering Response: Follow-up on Acceptance + Metrics
response_body.body:
Responding to the acceptance checklist and metrics correction.

1) Integration testing status: we completed endpoint verification in staging and agree the acceptance window still requires QA sign-off, per the checklist. We will not introduce schema changes during 07/15-07/17.
2) Metrics: we confirm the “Success Rate” miscomparison was due to the session vs gateway denominator. Engineering agrees to report using the new definition from 07/18 onward.

We need delivery to update the rollout narrative accordingly so Support and CS are not using conflicting numbers.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Status Alignment (Final for Leadership)
response_body.body:
Leadership alignment — consolidated for Project Alpha.

Resolved status after the metrics definition correction (07/18):
- Engineering: core APIs are stable in staging; QA acceptance is still required but can proceed per checklist.
- Delivery: integration acceptance window is confirmed for 07/15-07/17; rollout messaging will use the corrected “Success Rate” definition.
- Support: runbooks are in draft; final top-5 issue list will be ready by 07/22; staffing coverage is being prepared pending rollout date confirmation.
- Customer Success: training and migration assistance messaging is pending leadership confirmation for content format (recorded+live vs live-only) and the escalation owner.

Proposed rollout readiness target: after QA sign-off + final support/CS enablement.

Please confirm the following items by 07/24 COB: (1) training format and escalation owner (2) definitive rollout date after QA sign-off (3) approved customer communication language referencing corrected metrics.

response_body.subject: Re: Project Alpha Support Runbook Draft — Migration Assistance Workflow
response_body.body:
Support runbook draft is ready for migration assistance workflow.
- Includes escalation ladder and expected response times.
- Covers “export throttling” and “WebSocket reconnect” with mitigation steps.

We still need one decision from leadership: who owns the customer escalation after the first 2 assistance cycles (Support vs CS). Once confirmed, we can finalize the customer-facing instructions.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha (FYI): Policy update on access controls
response_body.body: Access control policy update for Project Alpha-related services. Please review by next week.

response_body.subject: Alphaware Update: Marketing dashboard status
response_body.body: This is about Alphaware (a different internal initiative). It should be ignored when producing Project Alpha reporting.

## 1) Project Overview
Project Alpha is preparing for integration acceptance by QA and an associated customer rollout. Core APIs are considered stable in staging, but the work is gated on completing the QA integration acceptance checklist (07/15–07/17). Stakeholders also corrected a critical metrics-definition discrepancy (“Success Rate”) to ensure all reporting uses the same denominator going forward.

## 2) Role-based progress
### Delivery
- Confirmed the integration acceptance window is **07/15–07/17**, contingent on QA sign-off.
- Emphasizes that if QA sign-off slips, the customer rollout date may need adjustment.
- Requests: stable integration test environment + exact QA handoff checklist so Delivery can coordinate readiness with Support.

### Engineering
- Reports **core API surface stabilized in staging by 07/06**, with primary endpoint integration test runs completed (auth, metrics read, export).
- Remaining engineering work described as documentation polish and alert threshold tightening.
- Agrees to honor the QA checklist window by **not introducing schema changes during 07/15–07/17**.
- Confirms agreement on the **corrected “Success Rate” metrics definition** for stakeholder reporting.

### Support
- Expresses concern about post-launch readiness: expected ticket/incidents spike in the first 72 hours.
- Notes runbook gaps initially (export throttling + WebSocket reconnect behavior, customer troubleshooting flow).
- Later update: **migration assistance support runbook draft is ready**, covering export throttling and WebSocket reconnect mitigations.
- Still needs one leadership decision: **who owns customer escalation after the first two assistance cycles** (Support vs Customer Success).

### Customer Success (CS)
- Customer calls are progressing, but CS indicates internal messaging inconsistency (different timelines heard from different teams).
- CS needs clarity on:
  - training format (**recorded + live Q&A** vs **live-only**),
  - migration assistance window length and escalation owner,
  - an aligned readiness message to avoid contradicting customers.
- Adds an operational gating: if alignment isn’t achieved by **07/13**, CS would pause new scheduling to prevent inconsistent messaging.

## 3) Dependencies and Risks
### Key dependencies
- **QA integration acceptance sign-off** (gating item)
  - Delivery/rollout timing depends on QA running the checklist during **07/15–07/17** and completing sign-off.
  - Engineering has committed not to introduce schema changes in that window, but QA’s schedule is still the critical path.
- **Leadership decisions to finalize customer-facing enablement**
  - Support runbook is draft-ready, but escalation ownership after the first two assistance cycles requires leadership confirmation.
  - CS training format + escalation owner + approved customer communication language require leadership alignment.

### Explicit risks / potential blockers
- **Acceptance delay risk**
  - If QA sign-off slips, Delivery flags the **rollout date adjustment** risk.
- **Runbook/customer workflow completeness risk**
  - Support initially lacked final runbook components and customer troubleshooting flow; mitigated by the later draft runbook update, but final escalation ownership is still pending.
- **Metrics/reporting inconsistency risk (addressed)**
  - Earlier emails compared different denominators for “Success Rate,” which could lead to incorrect conclusions about readiness/stability.
- **Customer messaging contradiction risk**
  - CS reports customers received conflicting timelines from internal teams; mitigated by leadership alignment and the corrected rollout narrative, but final confirmation is still requested.

## 4) Items requiring executive/management confirmation (actionable)
At least 3 items explicitly requested in the retrieved emails:
1) **Training format confirmation** for CS: recorded + live Q&A vs live-only (requested by CS / consolidated for leadership).
2) **Definitive rollout date after QA sign-off** (Delivery gated; leadership asked to confirm by 07/24 COB).
3) **Approved customer communication language** referencing the **corrected “Success Rate”** definition (to prevent conflicting readiness claims).
4) **Customer escalation ownership after first two assistance cycles**: whether Support or CS owns the escalation (Support runbook update calls out this exact missing decision).
5) (Also called out) **Final top-5 issue list timing/acceptance** readiness package (Support indicates runbook top issues final list ready by 07/22, pending rollout-date confirmation).

## 5) Current Status (single aligned final narrative)
**Reconciliation of role disagreements (at least two):**
1) **Metrics discrepancy vs reported stability readiness**
   - Earlier comparisons implied different interpretations of “Success Rate” (gateway-log denominator vs session/auth denominator).
   - **Resolution:** The “metrics definition changed / correction” email establishes the new definition:
     - Old: successful events / all observed gateway events
     - New: successful user sessions / total authenticated sessions (excluding failed auth)
   - Engineering confirms the correction; Delivery/Leadership alignment explicitly states rollout narrative uses the corrected definition. This resolves inconsistent readiness interpretation.

2) **Rollout enablement completeness and messaging**
   - Support initially reported **runbook gaps** and incomplete customer troubleshooting flow; CS also flagged **conflicting timelines** being communicated to customers.
   - **Resolution:** Support subsequently provided a migration assistance runbook draft including export throttling and WebSocket reconnect mitigations, but still requires leadership to decide escalation ownership after the first two cycles. Leadership consolidation also states CS messaging readiness is **pending leadership confirmation** of training format and escalation owner. This resolves “support not ready” vs “support is drafting” into: support is draft-ready, but final customer instructions depend on one final leadership decision and CS enablement alignment.

**Unified final status:**
- **Engineering:** Core APIs are stable in staging; endpoint verification is complete. Engineering will avoid schema changes during QA acceptance (07/15–07/17).
- **QA / Delivery gating:** Integration is **not yet accepted by QA**, and the acceptance checklist will be executed during **07/15–07/17**. Final acceptance is the gate for the confirmed customer rollout date.
- **Support:** Migration assistance runbook is in draft form and covers the key mitigation areas (export throttling + WebSocket reconnect), but final customer-facing escalation ownership after the first two assistance cycles is pending leadership confirmation.
- **Customer Success:** CS is prepared to proceed with training/migration assistance communications, but customer messaging is intentionally withheld/paused for new scheduling requests until leadership confirms training format and escalation owner and approves corrected communication language tied to the updated “Success Rate” definition.

**Aligned takeaway:** Project Alpha is **ready at the engineering core level**, but rollout readiness is **actively gated by QA integration acceptance (07/15–07/17)** plus **final leadership decisions** needed to fully align Support and CS enablement and customer communications.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Delivery Update: Integration Acceptance Window
response_body.body:
Team, as of today Project Alpha integration is NOT yet accepted by QA. Engineering says core APIs are ready, but the integration acceptance window is still open: we have to complete verification of event flows end-to-end (orders -> dashboard -> webhooks). Proposed acceptance window: 07/15-07/17. If QA sign-off slips, our customer rollout will need a date adjustment.

Next steps: please confirm the integration test environment is stable and provide the exact checklist for the handoff so delivery can coordinate with support for readiness.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Engineering Check-in: Core APIs Stabilized
response_body.body:
Good news: by 07/06 the core API surface for Project Alpha is stable in staging. We completed integration test runs for the primary endpoints (auth + metrics read + export). No new regressions after the last WebSocket gateway patch.

Remaining engineering work is limited to documentation polish and tightening alert thresholds. Engineering can support the integration acceptance checklist, but we need delivery to lock the QA window so we can staff on-call.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Support Concern: Post-Launch Ticket Volume Prep
response_body.body:
We’re worried about support readiness for Project Alpha launch. Based on prior dashboards, we expect a spike in migration/help requests and incident reports during the first 72 hours.

Current gaps:
- We do not yet have the runbook for “export endpoint throttling” and “WebSocket reconnect behavior”.
- The customer-facing troubleshooting flow is not final.
- We need confirmation on the estimated rollout timing so we can ensure on-call coverage and training.

Please share: rollout schedule + the top 5 known issues with mitigations.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Customer Success Sync: Training & Migration Assistance
response_body.body:
CS update: customer calls are progressing for Project Alpha, but we need an early confirmation on training + migration help.

What we told customers:
- Training sessions start the week before rollout.
- Migration assistance is included for the first two cycles.

What we still need internally:
1) confirm whether training is “recorded + live Q&A” or live-only
2) confirm the migration assistance window (days) and who provides escalation
3) align on one message for readiness: customers are hearing different timelines from different internal teams.

If we can’t align by 07/13, CS will pause new scheduling requests to avoid contradicting messaging.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Comms: Shared Uptime Dashboard Link
response_body.body:
FYI for Project Alpha stakeholders: the shared uptime dashboard is https://alpha-status.mycompany.internal (requires SSO). Please use it as the single source of truth for incident monitoring during rollout.

If you see discrepancies, escalate with timestamp + service name so we can correlate. Do not base ticket volume assumptions on internal estimates alone.

response_body.subject: Re: Project Alpha Integration Acceptance — Checklist Details
response_body.body:
Acceptance checklist for Project Alpha integration (for QA sign-off):
- Auth handshake completes for 3 test tenants
- Metrics read returns correct counts for baseline dataset
- Export endpoint returns expected file format for 2 scenarios
- WebSocket gateway reconnect within 10s recovers stream
- Audit log entries exist for all actions above

We can run the checklist during 07/15-07/17 as long as staging remains consistent. Please ensure Engineering does not introduce schema changes during this window.

response_body.subject: Metrics Definition Correction: Project Alpha “Success Rate” Calculation
response_body.body:
Correction / alignment notice (important): our previously reported “Success Rate” for Project Alpha used an inconsistent metrics definition.

What changed:
- Old definition (used in earlier status emails): Success Rate = successful events / all events observed in gateway logs.
- New definition (now adopted): Success Rate = successful user sessions / total authenticated sessions (excludes failed auth).

Impact:
- The old metric will look lower in environments with auth failures.
- Engineering’s staging numbers and Support’s production ticket correlates were comparing different denominators.

Going forward:
- Use the new definition for all stakeholder reporting.
- When discussing stability, separate “API success” from “session success”.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Engineering Response: Follow-up on Acceptance + Metrics
response_body.body:
Responding to the acceptance checklist and metrics correction.

1) Integration testing status: we completed endpoint verification in staging and agree the acceptance window still requires QA sign-off, per the checklist. We will not introduce schema changes during 07/15-07/17.
2) Metrics: we confirm the “Success Rate” miscomparison was due to the session vs gateway denominator. Engineering agrees to report using the new definition from 07/18 onward.

We need delivery to update the rollout narrative accordingly so Support and CS are not using conflicting numbers.

response_body.subject: Project Alpha Status Alignment (Final for Leadership)
response_body.body:
Leadership alignment — consolidated for Project Alpha.

Resolved status after the metrics definition correction (07/18):
- Engineering: core APIs are stable in staging; QA acceptance is still required but can proceed per checklist.
- Delivery: integration acceptance window is confirmed for 07/15-07/17; rollout messaging will use the corrected “Success Rate” definition.
- Support: runbooks are in draft; final top-5 issue list will be ready by 07/22; staffing coverage is being prepared pending rollout date confirmation.
- Customer Success: training and migration assistance messaging is pending leadership confirmation for content format (recorded+live vs live-only) and the escalation owner.

Proposed rollout readiness target: after QA sign-off + final support/CS enablement.

Please confirm the following items by 07/24 COB: (1) training format and escalation owner (2) definitive rollout date after QA sign-off (3) approved customer communication language referencing corrected metrics.

We still need one decision from leadership: who owns the customer escalation after the first 2 assistance cycles (Support vs CS). Once confirmed, we can finalize the customer-facing instructions.
